messages:
mike: Heads-up — brought up q-rerank-3b-v2 (GPT-style reranker quantized to int8/PTQ) on the dev harness. Global NDCG ~on-par with fp32, but seeing a 6-8% MRR drop specifically on Japanese queries. Anyone seen localized MRR-only regressions like this?

anna: ouch. do we have a subset breakdown by dataset? jp vs en, longdoc vs passage?

jess: quick snapshot: eval run command below (ran on latest eval-harness):
```bash
python eval.py --model q-rerank-3b-v2 --tasks webqa_jp,docs_jp,webqa_en --metric mrr,ndcg@10 --tokenizer tok-v2 --quant int8 --batch 64
```
results: webqa_jp MRR -0.07, ndcg@10 -0.01; webqa_en MRR +0.01 ndcg +0.00

mike: interesting that ndcg is stable. suggests top-k swap behaviour, not gross relevance drop.

ryan: did we apply any query/doc formatting changes for jp? e.g., strip HTML tags or normalize punctuation? those can change tokenization heavily for ja.

diana: yes — the new preproc has a small change: we added an XML stripper for docs to remove <code> blocks. Might be aggressive on japanese text where punctuation sits next to characters.

anna: can we repro by toggling the stripper? run eval with --preproc strip_tags=true/false and compare.

jess: ran that. disabling tag-stripper -> webqa_jp MRR recovers to -0.01 vs fp32. So it's largely the preproc change interacting with quantized model.

mike: so two variables: quantization + preproc. Could be tokenization boundary shift causing reranker to move the highest-scoring doc out of top1.

ryan: add the tokenizer normalization flag too: some tokenizers collapse fullwidth punctuation differently. Try --tokenizer-normalize=ja.

jess: done. with normalize_ja=true + strip_tags=false -> MRR delta ~ +0.00 (matches fp32). normalize_ja=true + strip_tags=true -> MRR -0.02.

diana: hypothesis: tag stripper is merging tokens across tag boundaries causing slightly different prefix-kv states, and quantization amplifies small score shifts.

mike: ok. we should: 1) add a per-query-length and per-intent slice (short Q vs long Q, navigational vs informational) 2) run sign-test on top1 swaps 3) run 2-bit-int4 PTQ (if available) to see amplification trend

anna: i'll add slices. quick note: top1 swaps are mostly head queries (len<=8 chars) and many are exact-match-like. small tokenization shift can flip ranks.

ryan: can you post an example pair where fp32 picked A and int8 picked B?

jess: yes, example thread:
- query: "新宿 カレー おすすめ"
- fp32 top1 doc: "〜新宿で人気のカレー店…" (contains the phrase exactly)
- int8 top1 doc: "新宿の老舗カレー屋レビュー" (semantically similar by embedding but slightly broader)

mike: semantic vs exact-match — reranker scoring margin small. need to check token-level scores for those two docs. can we diff logits/score components?

jess: i pulled raw scores. fp32 score(A)=3.12, score(B)=3.07. int8 score(A)=3.01, score(B)=3.09. so A drops more under int8. margin shift ~0.1.

diana: interesting that A lost more. maybe particular token embedding quant errors for some Japanese Kanji sequences. We should run a stable-seed microbench: identical prompt, just run many times to check nondeterminism.

mike: also file a bug for evaluation harness: make tag-stripping opt-in per-locale. We shouldn't globally rewrite ja docs unless validated.

anna: +1. I'll open a quick PR to toggle stripper by locale and add tests.

ryan: for actionables:
- jess: run int4-ptq and full-fp16 on same preproc toggles and produce per-slice ndcg/mrr + top1 swap list (limit 50) — due EOD
- diana: investigate tokenizer normalization differences and add microtoken tests for common jp phrases — due tomorrow
- anna: PR to make stripper locale-aware + unit tests — WIP
- mike: coordinate a quick eval sign-test with product-owner for deciding rollback if user-visible top1 regressions >5%

jess: starting run now. posting interim bot summary when done.

eval-bot: Eval finished for q-rerank-3b-v2 (int8) on 2024-05-05T14:28Z — aggregate: NDCG@10 delta -0.003, MRR delta -0.065 on webqa_jp. Top1 swap count: 128/2000 (6.4%). Seeded reruns stable within 0.01.

mike: thanks. this is actionable. preferring localized preproc toggle + deeper quant checks before rollback. :thumbsup:

anna: will sync on the call at 16:00 to decide rollout plan.
